newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher on late local rally.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher on late local rally.

text.p: COMEX copper rallied on the close on local short-covering triggering light stops and catching the funds short, raising the prospect of a further rally Friday.
The hedge funds were believed to be short and holding when a spree of local buying jolting the market out of its tight range.
The September contract was 107.80 cents a pound, up 2.20 cents from Wednesday, while the spot month was up 2.00 cents to 109.90 cents a pound.
"The locals hit some light stops, but volumes weren't huge, so it didn't take much to move the market," said Tony Ellis, a trader with Gerald Brokerage.
"The funds are still short," he added. "But if the price moves any higher, we could see them start to cover."
One floor trader said earlier that if September prices break key resistance at 110.00 cents, the funds could sent covering.

"There was nothing fundamental ion the market," said William O'Neill, senior futures strategist with Merrill Lynch. "Aluminum and zinc were a little stronger today. That lent some strength to the market."

The market had several reasons to be bearish. The London Metal Exchange cash-to-three-month backwardation was $48/$53, narrower from Wednesday. And LME stocks continue its climb with another 3,950-tonne increase to 204,900 tonnes, the highest level since March 10.
Dealers also noted that the COMEX August-September spread moved into a 0.20-cent contango. "That would appear to remove the threat of any near-term tightness," one trade broker said.

The nearby months were weight down early in response to the issuance of 650 delivery notices by Cargill, who were believed to be representing a U.K. bank. By the end of the session, the delivery notices were discounted.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
